# <span id="aanchor245"></span> Calculated Meter Editor

Currently, FLOWCAL only supports gas calculated meters.

A calculated meter (also called a virtual or pseudo meter) is a meter that does not physically exist but is calculated from known meter values. The total volume, mass and energy for a calculated meter are determined based on meter member contributions during the period in which they were added. You can also set up a conditional statement with basic arithmetic operations and absolute values to specify member contributions.

A calculated meter may also be used to determine how much analysis component volume is lost in a balanced system. This application is important because the amount of certain gases emitted into the environment must be documented and submitted to the government.

Texas is a segment location within a system, comprising many meters. You want to know the volume entering Harris County where a physical meter does not exist. You can calculate that volume using upstream meters as data points (a calculated meter).

</div>

 

<div class="procedure">

To access the Calculated Meter Editor:

Go to **Setup** \> **Meter** \> **Calculated Meter**.



<img src="data:image/png;base64," class="ScreenShot" style="width: 600;height: 600;" />

</div>

<a href="javascript:void(0);" class="MCToggler MCTogglerHead MCTogglerHotSpot MCToggler_Open toggler MCTogglerHotSpot_ MCHotSpotImage" data-mc-targets="Details">

<img src="data:image/gif;base64," class="MCToggler_Image_Icon" data-mc-alt2="Open" width="16" height="11" alt="Closed" />Calculated Meter Editor Details</a>

<div class="drop-down" style="display: none;" mc-target-name="Details">

The following items are available in the Calculated Meter Editor screen:

- **Calc Meter/Name** - Calculated meter number and name

- **System** - FLOWCAL System the calculated meter is associated with

- **Unknown Volume** - A user may find that the sign on an unknown value, once calculated, is negative. To correct this, FLOWCAL has created an option called Unknown Volume, which simply changes the sign of the result of the unknown volume equation. While a value yielded from an unknown volume calculation may be accurate as a negative number, some accounting departments require that figures be entered with positive numbers and identify whether the value is inlet or outlet via the configuration.

- **Fix PPAs** - Every PPA record written (table fc_ppa_accounting_info) for a meter is also written for any parent calculated meters. Before the ability to purge PPAs was introduced, this was often done with SQL scripts. At times the calculated meter was overlooked. This button does a force delete and re-copy of the calculated meter’s PPA from its members when backing out PPAs for member meters.

  This feature is usually only requested by FLOWCAL Support.

- **Reference Meter** - Used to ensure common pressure base, temperature base, contract hour and contract day for all meters in a calculated meter.

  The reference meter is dependent on the From/To Date values and can change for each relationship time frame.

- **From/To** - Start and end datetime, which represents each time frame the members have been included within the calculated meter. In the To field, the maximum date can be entered by pressing **Ctrl+E** and the minimum date in the From field can be entered by pressing **Ctrl+S**. The end date must be greater than the start date.

- **Formulas** - Read-only field that displays whether the formula is enabled for the current datetime span. (See: [Formulas tab](Formulas%20Tab.md))

- **Find** - Open the find tool to search members of a calculated meter

- **Refresh** - Refresh the screen

- **Security** - View or edit users that have access to the calculated meter.

  User/group access to calculated meters is only relevant for companies that maintain object level security. Most companies do not restrict access at the object level.

- **Delete** - Delete a calculated meter.

- **Edit** - Enable edit mode for the calculated meter.

- **New** - Create a new calculated meter. When you click the **New** button, the fluid phase is set to the user-defined default fluid phase configured within User Preferences. To set the fluid phase manually, click the drop-down on the **New** button and select "Gas" or "Liquid".

- **Exit** - Close Calculated Meter Editor.

- **Query** - Open the Query Editor to populate the Calculated Meter based on a query. To add members based on a query, run the query from the Query Editor and select the members from the list of query results by clicking the right arrow button.

- **Save** - Save your changes.

- **Cancel** - Discard your changes.

</div>
